title: The Global Water Crisis: Why We're Running Out

lines: Clean water from a tap seems endless.
But controlling water has shaped civilization.
Today, 7 in 10 people have running water.
Yet many cities face critical shortages.
slides.keyIdea: Access to clean water has been central to human civilization and development.

lines: Cape Town nearly ran out of water.
Four million people faced shutoff taps.
São Paulo, Melbourne, Jakarta, and others
will hit their own crisis within decades.
slides.keyIdea: Multiple major cities worldwide face imminent water supply crises.

lines: Earth has 326 million trillion gallons.
But 97% is salty, 2% is frozen.
Humans rely on just 1% of water.
Access depends heavily on where you live.
slides.keyIdea: Earth has abundant water, but only a tiny fraction is usable freshwater.

lines: Mexico City drained its lakes centuries ago.
Now it pumps groundwater unsustainably.
The city will lose half its water
supply within 30 to 50 years.
slides.keyIdea: Overuse of groundwater depletes aquifers that took millennia to fill.

lines: Drinking uses only 8% of freshwater.
Agriculture and industry use the rest.
One hamburger requires 1,650 liters.
Global meat consumption keeps rising.
slides.keyIdea: Hidden water in food production drives most freshwater consumption.

lines: Water is priced too cheaply everywhere.
Farmers pay almost nothing for it.
Mexico City loses half its water to leaks.
We dump 2 million tons of waste daily.
slides.keyIdea: Underpricing water encourages waste and prevents infrastructure investment.

lines: Water scarcity drives violent conflict.
Darfur's crisis killed hundreds of thousands.
Syria's drought contributed to civil war.
Competition for water intensifies globally.
slides.keyIdea: Water scarcity fuels geopolitical tensions and armed conflicts worldwide.

lines: Water is a human right, not commodity.
Cape Town cut usage in half through action.
Recognize water's value before it's gone.
Individual choices and awareness matter.
slides.keyIdea: Treating water as invaluable and acting urgently can prevent crisis.
